title: Describing a room: no van needed

sections.content: When the predicate is an adjective, 3rd-person present drops van entirely: A nappali világos. (The living room is bright.) — NOT A nappali van világos. This is the same zero-copula pattern you met early on with nouns; it works for adjectives too.

items.english: The living room is bright and cozy.

sections.content: The urge to add van here is strong for English speakers, since 'is' feels essential. Resist it: van appears in this kind of sentence only for location or existence, never as a bare linking word before an adjective.
